{{Quote|One result might be giantism, well beyond the Pau'an norm.|11-4D|<ref name="DP" />}}
'''Giantism''' or '''gigantism''' was a medical deformity which resulted in a being growing far larger than the norm. Low [[theloxin]] levels in a [[Pau'an/Legends|Pau'an]] would possibly result in this. [[11-4D/Legends|11-4D]] knew this when inquired as to by [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]].<ref name="DP" /> Similar results could also be achieved chemically, as was the case with [[Erdan/Legends|Erdan]], a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] who had been artificially enlarged by his owner.<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|239|Erdan}}</ref> The former [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] and [[Prophets of the Dark Side]] named [[Jedgar]] was a Human giant, measuring 2.3 [[Meter/Legends|meters]]<ref name="PLH" /> while his species averaged 1.8 meters.<ref name="RPGRCR">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Revised Core Rulebook]]''</ref> By abuse of language, the word "giant" was also used to describe bigger [[Subspecies/Legends|breeds]] within a given species, such as the [[giant thranta]],<ref name="WoSW">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref> or even a species in which greater size was normal, such as the [[Wyyyschokk/Legends|Kashyyykian giant weaver]].<ref name="TFUn">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed'' novelization]]</ref> Additionally, species that were far larger than most [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] were often referred to as giants, including the extinct [[Gargantelle]]s of [[Boz Pity/Legends|Boz Pity]], whose statures topped twenty meters,<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> and the [[B'rknaa]] of [[Indobok]].<ref name="SWDK4">[[Droids (1994) 4|''Droids'' (1994) 4]]</ref>
